editor_spans.body: The speech contains something the press release the day before left out: an offer of 'DWP devolution', meaning employment support designed by Holyrood. That is the first real concession in the Prime Minister's approach to Scotland. Until now the offer was a request that the Scottish Government give power away. Now Westminster is putting one of its own powers on the table. The order looks deliberate. Holyrood gets a share of the welfare system, which the SNP has long wanted, and in return it is asked to let Scottish regions have power too.

There is a tension in the speech's own terms. The Prime Minister says deep devolution is 'not swapping power from one parliament to another'. Yet the one concrete offer moves employment support from Westminster to Holyrood. Going lower than that depends on a condition the UK cannot enforce: the support has to follow the 'Easterhouse principle' of names not numbers, or 'it won't work'. Once the power belongs to Holyrood, whether it reaches estates like Easterhouse is Holyrood's choice. London can only argue for it. That fits what we wrote last week: in Scotland this Prime Minister has influence over Holyrood but no power to direct it.

The examples he chose say more than the rhetoric does. They are Ravenscraig, closed by people 'hundreds of miles away', Leigh after the pits, and Greater Manchester's buses built in Falkirk because a few extra pounds kept the money in Britain. Each one treats deindustrialisation as something the centre did, and buying British as something a well-run local body can fix. The national promises are much less specific: a 'new deal' on farming at the 20 November summit, unnamed help for Grangemouth, more to say about Aberdeen 'in due course'. The test of the speech is the National Economic Council in a few weeks' time, its first meeting with the devolved First Ministers under this Prime Minister. It will show whether the DWP offer comes with money and a timetable, or only a principle.

S352 (mentioning Andy Burnham {Q269909}, Scotland’s First Minister {E420}, Parliament of the United Kingdom {Q11010}, Scottish Parliament {Q206171}): In a speech today, the Prime Minister will invite Scotland’s First Minister to work with ⟦Andy Burnham⟧ on the common good of pushing more power out of both Westminster and Holyrood, unlocking jobs and opportunity in every region.
S353 (mentioning Lanarkshire {Q530296}, Andy Burnham {Q269909}, Scottish Government {Q32521}, Scottish Parliament {Q206171}, Parliament of the United Kingdom {Q11010}): Delivering ⟦Andy Burnham’s⟧ remarks after speaking with young people today in Lanarkshire, Andy Burnham will emphasise the Scottish Government is one of the most centralised devolved administrations in Europe, with Holyrood not giving people who know their areas best enough of a say, despite significant devolution from Westminster over the last 27 years.
S354 (mentioning Andy Burnham {Q269909}, Scottish Parliament {Q206171}): Because power was never supposed to stop at the doors of the Scottish Parliament, the Prime Minister will argue the next stage of devolution should place more decision-making in the hands of Scotland’s regions and cities to drive reindustrialisation.
S355 (mentioning Andy Burnham {Q269909}, Scottish Government {Q32521}, Government of the United Kingdom {Q6063}, Number 10 North {Q140382294}, Scotland Office {Q277020}, Scotland {Q22}): As part of that offer, ⟦Andy Burnham⟧ will call on the Scottish Government to work with the UK Government through No10 North and the Scotland Office to develop a new model of regional empowerment for Scotland, ensuring communities with their own strengths, identity and ambitions can seize new economic opportunities and unlock their potential.
S370 (spoken by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, mentioning Scotland’s First Minister {E420}): During my first week in office, I told the First Minister that I wanted to work with ⟦Scotland’s First Minister⟧ to spread opportunities to communities across Scotland’s regions and cities.
S396 (spoken by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, mentioning Number 10 North {Q140382294}): Through No10 North, we are rewiring the state and I want to make sure regions in Scotland are fully part of this.
S397 (spoken by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, mentioning Scottish Government {Q32521}): This is me making an offer to the Scottish Government.
S398 (spoken by Prime Minister Andy Burnham): With us working together, there is no limit to what we can achieve for the Scottish people.
S400 (spoken by Douglas Alexander, mentioning Scottish Parliament {Q206171}): Devolution has done a great deal, but power was never supposed to stop at the doors of the Scottish Parliament.
S371 (spoken by Douglas Alexander, mentioning North Lanarkshire {Q207111}, Fife {Q201149}, THE HIGHLANDS {Q134995225}, London {Q84}, Edinburgh {Q23436}): People in North Lanarkshire, in Fife or in the Highlands know what their communities need better than any minister, whether they sit in London or Edinburgh.
S356 (spoken by Douglas Alexander, mentioning Andy Burnham {Q269909}, Scottish Government {Q32521}, Scotland Office {Q277020}): The Prime Minister’s offer to the Scottish Government is a genuine one, and the Scotland Office is ready to roll up its sleeves alongside ⟦Scottish Government⟧ to make it happen.
